answer: Persistent workload relic: each identity must periodically solve a unique, memory-hard task whose solution chain is checkpointed to a slow shared island of archival nodes. Skipping a checkpoint voids the chain, forcing recomputation from genesis. Cloning N identities multiplies steady-state compute and storage N-fold, since each clone needs its own chain, while honest agents amortize one. A lotus flag marks verified chains for priority routing.
